Subject: Post-call: Searchlytics embedding fit checklist & next steps

Hi Hyejin / Ravi — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap + recommended next steps so we have alignment on model fit, benchmarks, and risk areas for your semantic search pilot.

Key takeaways from discovery:
- Primary objective: improve fresh content recall for 0–14 day documents and reduce false positives for similar legal snippets.
- Data shape: ~1.2M docs total, initial pilot: 100k subset filtered by recency and topic (we have a 1k sample attached).
- Latency target: P50 < 35ms embedding lookup; throughput target: 500 qps during peak indexing.
- Concern: you surface drift and dimensionality artifacts when documents include long boilerplate (legal headers).

Recommended evaluation plan (short):
1) Models to try (ranked):
   - redwood-embed-sim-2.0 (dense, 1k-d vectors) — good baseline for legal-style semantic similarity
   - redwood-embed-quant-lite (384-d, 8-bit quant) — cost-efficient candidate if recall loss is small
   - open-embed-large-v1 (1k-d) — control to validate upper-bound recall

2) Benchmarks/metrics to run (we prepared scripts):
   - MRR@10, Recall@100, cosine-sim distribution by doc length buckets
   - dimensionality: mean pairwise cosine variance and PCA explained variance for top-10 components
   - drift check: compare sample (current) vs last-90-days token distributions and embedding centroid shifts

3) Prompt/Normalization guidance (MAP prompt set attached):
   - Strip boilerplate headers; feed the cleaned text field for embedding only
   - Use 512-token truncation for queries, 2048 token window for docs with weighted windowing for long boilerplate

4) Risks & mitigations:
   - Dimensionality collapse for the quant model: run PCA explained-variance check and measure cluster separability on labeled query set. If cluster overlap > 0.25 AUC drop, fallback to full-precision model.
   - Drift: schedule weekly small-batch re-embeds for new content and monitor centroid distance; if centroid shift > 0.12 cosine, trigger human review

Action items / next steps:
- Redwood: run two model comparisons across your 1k sample and return bench report by EOD Thu (we attached a starter report). (Owner: Karthik)
- Searchlytics: send a second 5k sample focused on recent law updates and mark 50 queries for labeled relevance. (Owner: Hyejin)
- Joint: 30-minute sync next Tue to review quantitative results + mutual action plan for pilot.

Attachments: searchlytics-sample-1000.json, embed-benchmark-report-20270713.pdf, MAP_prompt_set_v1.txt

Thanks — happy to iterate.

—
Marissa Cole

Hi all — quick technical notes following Marissa’s plan: 

On vector dims and quantization:
- The quantized candidate is configurable; we can generate 384/512 vectors from the same checkpoint during offline benching. Cost uplift from 384->512 is ~18% in token-stage compute for indexing only.
- Suggest we include a 512-d quant run as a third column in the bench matrix; sometimes legal text benefits from slightly higher dimensionality to capture subtle token co-occurrence.

On dimensionality metrics to add:
- Add silhouette score on labeled queries (NMI also useful if you have coarse topic buckets).
- Compare explained variance ratio for first 20 PCA components; if cumulative variance < 0.35 at 20 comps for the quant model, it's a red flag.

On deployment and drift mitigation:
- For the pilot, enable prefix/KV caching on indexes of frequently-updated docs (e.g., press releases) — reduces re-embed cost for small edits.
- We'll produce a small script to compute centroid-distance and explain the thresholding so you can onboard this into Searchlytics monitoring.

Deliverables I’ll run by EOD Thu:
- bench CSV (MRR, Recall, silhouette, PCA_variance columns)
- short README for the MAP prompt normalization steps

—Karthik
